# MCP Server

Official MrScraper MCP server for retrieving web pages, web search, and account usage. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally.

MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper.
It connects AI clients to web page retrieval, web search, and your account
usage.

The server exposes seven tools:

Use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint for a managed connection, or run the
published MCP package locally through Streamable HTTP or stdio.

Package information

This page documents `@mrscraper/mcp` version **0.5.0**. Its seven tools share their descriptions, inputs, and defaults with the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. 0.5.0 replaced `scraperAPI` with `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, and `getScreenshot`, added `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson`, renamed the inputs to camel case, and changed the OAuth scopes. See Migration from the previous tool set.

## Capabilities

### Page Retrieval

Retrieve a known URL as HTML, Markdown, or a screenshot, with optional
browser rendering, real-device routing, proxy controls, selector waiting,
and retry limits.

### Brand and JSON Extraction

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links, or
structured JSON from a natural-language prompt.

### Web Search

Search the web for ranked results, for a chosen country and up to 100
results at a time.

### Account Status

Read the subscription, token limit, token usage, remaining tokens, and rate
limit.

### Managed Endpoint

Connect to the hosted MCP endpoint through Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1
browser sign-in.

### Structured Tool Results

Receive a consistent response envelope in MCP structured content.

### Interactive Widgets

Render search results and an account usage meter in hosts that support MCP
Apps.

## Requirements

* A MrScraper account
* An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support
* An API key only when the client cannot use
  OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally

## Quick start with the hosted server

Add the hosted endpoint

Configure a Streamable HTTP server named `mrscraper` with no credential:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this exact URL, including the `/mcp` path.

Sign in

Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1
challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve
`scrape:read` for the six scraping and search tools and `account:read`
for `status`.

Reload and verify

Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list.
The connection should expose `status`, `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`,
`getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch`.

## Copyable AI setup prompt

```
Connect MrScraper MCP to this agent. Detect the current MCP client and use its native Streamable HTTP setup to add a server named mrscraper at exactly https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp with no static credential. Complete the OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in; if it does not start automatically, use the client's MCP login or authenticate command. Only if the client does not support OAuth, fall back to a MrScraper API key from https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens stored through the client's environment-variable or secret-storage mechanism and sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Reload the MCP client when required, then list the tools and confirm that status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, and webSearch are available.
```

## Client configuration

Add the hosted URL without a static `Authorization` header, then complete
browser sign-in when the client prompts you.

### Codex

```
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```

Codex uses OAuth by default for Streamable HTTP servers. If browser sign-in does
not start automatically, run `codex mcp login mrscraper`.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add \
  --transport http \
  --scope user \
  mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```

Open `/mcp` inside Claude Code and authenticate, or run
`claude mcp login mrscraper` from your shell.

To add MrScraper's three skills for page retrieval and web search along with
the server, install the MrScraper plugin for Claude Code instead:

```
claude plugin marketplace add mrscraper-com/mrscraper-claude-plugin
claude plugin install mrscraper@mrscraper-claude
```

The plugin is also listed on
ClaudePluginHub.

### Claude and Claude Desktop

Open the custom connector form

In a general Claude chat, select the **+** button below the input box, then
choose **Connectors → Add connector → Add custom connector**.

Add MrScraper

Enter `MrScraper` as the name and
`https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` as the MCP server URL, then select
**Continue**.

Sign in

Complete the MrScraper OAuth browser flow when Claude prompts you.

### Cursor

Open **Cursor Settings → Tools & MCP → Add Custom MCP**, then add:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Refresh the MCP server list, then authenticate when prompted.

### VS Code

Add the server to your user settings:

```
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "mrscraper": {
        "type": "http",
        "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For a workspace configuration, place the server object under `servers` in
`.vscode/mcp.json`. Start the server and VS Code opens a browser for OAuth.

### Windsurf

Add the following entry to the Windsurf MCP configuration:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Refresh the MCP server list, then complete OAuth when prompted.

### Other MCP clients

Use these connection values:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Name | `mrscraper` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| URL | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.1; do not configure a static header |

## API key fallback

If a client cannot complete OAuth, create an API key,
store it through the client's secret mechanism, and send it as a bearer token:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For Codex, pass the environment-variable name instead of embedding the key:

```
export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY="YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
```

## Authentication

| Connection | Credential source |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in, or an API key fallback |
| Self-hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 access token, or `Authorization: Bearer <MrScraper API key>` |
| Local stdio | `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`, then `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` |

The hosted server publishes OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and challenges
unauthenticated clients to start browser sign-in. Access tokens are issued for
the exact `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` resource. A tool called without its
required scope returns `403 insufficient_scope`, and your client can offer to
grant the missing permission.

| Scope | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| `scrape:read` | `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch` |
| `account:read` | `status` |

These are the only application scopes the server advertises; the
authorization server also offers `offline_access` for refresh tokens. Clients
take the scopes from the server's metadata, so don't pin scopes in client
configurations.

OAuth connections that already hold `scrape:read` keep working without
reconnecting; `scrape:write` is no longer needed by any tool. Connections
without `scrape:read` must reconnect and approve it to run the scraping and
search tools; `status` still uses `account:read`.

API keys remain supported for clients without OAuth and carry full account
authority, so no scope is enforced against them. Authentication stays at the
transport layer; tools never accept credentials as arguments.

## Run the MCP server locally

Node.js 20 or newer is required.

### Published package over stdio

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mrscraper/mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "MRSCRAPER_API_KEY": "YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Source checkout over Streamable HTTP

Clone and build

```
git clone https://github.com/mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp.git
cd mrscraper-mcp
npm ci
npm run build
```

Start HTTP transport

```
TRANSPORT=http npm start
```

The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`.

Connect the client

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Docker

```
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t mrscraper-mcp .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mrscraper-mcp
```

The image binds to `0.0.0.0`. Apply network controls appropriate for the
deployment and keep bearer verification enabled.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANSPORT` | `stdio` | Selects `stdio` or `http`. |
| `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address; the Docker image uses `0.0.0.0`. |
| `PORT` | `8000` | HTTP listen port. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` | — | Primary stdio credential. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` | — | Alternative stdio credential, also used by the Python SDK. |
| `MRSCRAPER_HTTP_AUTH` | `1` | Enables HTTP bearer verification. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH` | `1` | Accepts OAuth 2.1 access tokens alongside API keys. |
| `MRSCRAPER_MCP_PUBLIC_URL` | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com` | Public origin; `<origin>/mcp` is the required token audience. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_ISSUER` | `https://api.app.mrscraper.com` | Authorization server issuer. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_JWKS_URL` | `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json` | Key set used to verify access tokens. |
| `MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | — | Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the HTTP server. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_BASE_URL` | MrScraper platform API | Platform endpoint override used by `status`. |
| `MRSCRAPER_FETCH_BASE_URL` | MrScraper Scraper API | Endpoint override used by the six scraping and search tools. |
| `MRSCRAPER_LOG_HTTP_PAYLOAD` | off | Enables trusted-environment request-body diagnostics. |
| `MRSCRAPER_LOG_HTTP_PAYLOAD_MAX` | `8192` | Maximum diagnostic payload length. |

## Security behavior

* HTTP authentication is enabled by default.
* Credential-bearing response headers are filtered from tool output.
* Credential metadata in scraping and search responses is redacted, and
  network errors redact signed query credentials.
* `status` preserves every field of the account status response body,
  including account identity and billing identifiers. Only credential-bearing
  response headers are removed.
* Browser-origin requests are accepted from trusted local origins, from
  `claude.ai` and `chatgpt.com`, and from exact
  values configured through `MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
* Tool calls receive the caller's authenticated OAuth token or API key through
  the MCP transport rather than through tool arguments.

## Choosing the right tool

| Starting point | Desired outcome | Tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A known URL | Raw HTML | `scrapeHtml` |
| A known URL | Markdown, or Markdown and HTML together | `scrapeMarkdown` |
| A known URL | A screenshot of the full page or top viewport | `getScreenshot` |
| A website | Colors, typography, logos, and social links | `scrapeBrand` |
| A known URL | Data extracted as JSON with a natural-language prompt | `scrapeJson` |
| A topic or keyword | Search result discovery | `webSearch` |
| An account | Plan, token usage, and remaining tokens | `status` |

A discovery workflow commonly uses `webSearch` first, followed by
`scrapeMarkdown` or `scrapeHtml` for the pages that will inform the answer.
Agents produce summaries, tables, and structured output from the retrieved
content, or call `scrapeJson` to have MrScraper extract the data.

### Migration from the previous tool set

Version 0.5.0 replaces the tools and inputs of version 0.4:

| Previous | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `scraperAPI` | `scrapeHtml` for raw HTML, `scrapeMarkdown` for Markdown (with `html: true`, Markdown and HTML), or `getScreenshot` for a screenshot. Brand and JSON extraction are the separate `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson` tools. |
| `scraperAPI` inputs `geo_code`, `proxy_country`, `browser_rendering`, `wait_for_selector`, `block_resources`, `max_retries`, and `home_page` | `geoCode`, `proxyCountry`, `browserRendering`, `waitForSelector`, `blockResources`, `maxRetries`, and `warmStart`. |
| `scraperAPI` inputs `use_proxy`, `bypass_proxy`, `cookie_jar`, `headers`, `token_cap`, `stream`, and `discard_token_secret` | Removed. |
| `webSearch` inputs `url`, `region`, `num_results`, and `timeout` | `query`, `country`, and `numResults`. `query` is search text; a search results URL is no longer read for its `q` parameter. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. |
| `status` summary fields, such as `token_remaining` and `usage_percent` | The raw account status body, with account details at `data.data`. |
| OAuth scopes `scrape:read` and `scrape:write` | `scrape:read` for all six scraping and search tools; `scrape:write` is no longer needed. `status` still uses `account:read`. |

Browser rendering no longer switches on automatically. It is off unless
`browserRendering` is true; `getScreenshot` always renders, and
`scrapeMarkdown` renders when `html` is true. The page timeout defaults to 300
seconds (was 120), and omitting `maxRetries` means no retry limit (was 3).
ChatGPT and Codex sign-ins, which got a reduced `scraperAPI` in 0.4, now
receive the same seven tools and inputs as every other client.

Start a new client session or reconnect so the client refreshes its tool list.
OAuth connections that already hold `scrape:read` keep working; others must
reconnect and approve it. API keys keep working without scope approval.

Versions before 0.2.0 exposed `fetch`, `scrape`, `serp`, `rerun`, `results`,
and `result`. Manage AI scrapers, reruns, and stored results in the
MrScraper dashboard.

## Common response envelope

Every tool returns the same envelope in MCP `structuredContent` and as
formatted JSON in a text content block:

```
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "[Formatted JSON matching structuredContent]"
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "status_code": 200,
    "data": "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>",
    "headers": {
      "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status_code` | number or `null` | HTTP status returned by the MrScraper service, or `null` when the request ends before an HTTP response arrives. |
| `data` | JSON value, string, or `null` | The API response body, as parsed JSON or text. Its field names are not converted. |
| `headers` | object | Response headers with credential-bearing headers filtered out. |
| `error` | string, when present | Request failure summary. |

`status` preserves the complete account status body without adding summary
fields.

### Error handling

HTTP and network failures set `isError: true` on the MCP tool result and
include `error` in the envelope. Network failures use `status_code: null`.
Invalid inputs, including inputs a tool does not define, are rejected before
any upstream call. Authentication and missing OAuth scopes are enforced by the
HTTP transport before a tool runs.

## Tool reference

Tool names, descriptions, inputs, and defaults match the MrScraper CLI, SDKs,
and integrations. Inputs use camel case and are sent to the API under the same
names. Tools authenticate through the MCP connection and do not accept a token
argument.

| Tool | Title | OAuth scope | `readOnlyHint` | `openWorldHint` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | Account Status | `account:read` | `true` | `false` |
| `scrapeHtml` | Scrape HTML | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `scrapeMarkdown` | Scrape Markdown | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `getScreenshot` | Get Screenshot | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `scrapeBrand` | Scrape Brand | `scrape:read` | `true` | `true` |
| `scrapeJson` | Scrape JSON | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `webSearch` | Web Search | `scrape:read` | `true` | `true` |

Every tool sets `destructiveHint: false`. `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`,
`getScreenshot`, and `scrapeJson` are not marked read-only because
`saveResult` can save their results to your dashboard. The six scraping and
search tools use tokens from your plan.

Examples use `https://example.com` as the sample target. Replace it for your
use case. Response examples show the envelope from `structuredContent`, with
selected keys and types observed in live API responses. Values are
placeholders; page content, base64 images, and arrays are abbreviated. Actual
responses may contain additional fields.

### Shared parameters

HTML, Markdown, screenshots, and JSON extraction share `url`, `timeout`,
`geoCode`, `proxyCountry`, `super`, `waitUntil`, `proxy`, `maxRetries`, and
`saveResult`. Page defaults are 300 seconds, US geolocation and proxy country,
real-device routing off, and dashboard saving off. Omitted retry limits mean no
limit.

HTML, Markdown, and screenshots additionally accept `blockResources`,
`waitForSelector`, and `returnCookie`. JSON extraction does not accept these
controls. Browser rendering is optional for HTML, Markdown, and JSON;
screenshots always enable it. Markdown with HTML also enables browser
rendering.

The six scraping and search tools send `GET` requests to the Scraper API with
their inputs as query parameters:

```
GET https://api.mrscraper.com
```

Each tool's table lists its complete inputs.

### `status`

Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields.

`status` takes no service parameters and calls:

```
GET https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts
```

The HTTP deadline is fixed at 600 seconds. It is not a service parameter.

#### Example

```
{
  "name": "status",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

#### Response

The API body contains message and data. Account details remain nested in data, including subscriptionItem and scraperAllowance. The response envelope therefore exposes account details at data.data. Sensitive response headers are removed.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "message": "Example response",
    "data": {
      "id": "ACCOUNT_ID",
      "tokenLimit": 100000,
      "tokenUsage": 2500,
      "stripeStatus": "active",
      "user": {
        "name": "Example user",
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "isVerified": true
      },
      "subscriptionItem": {
        "name": "Example plan",
        "tokenLimit": 100000
      },
      "scraperAllowance": {
        "remaining": 97500,
        "plans": [
          {
            "remaining": 97500
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `scrapeHtml`

Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional.

The request sets `html=true`, `markdown=false`, and `screenshot=false`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| `timeout` | integer | `300` | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| `geoCode` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| `proxyCountry` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| `super` | boolean | `false` | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| `waitUntil` | string: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle0`, `networkidle2` | `"domcontentloaded"` | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |
| `proxy` | string | Omitted | Custom proxy URL used to load the page. |
| `maxRetries` | integer | Omitted | Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. |
| `saveResult` | boolean | `false` | Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. |
| `blockResources` | boolean | `false` | Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. |
| `waitForSelector` | string | Omitted | Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. |
| `returnCookie` | boolean | `false` | Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. |
| `browserRendering` | boolean | `false` | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| `warmStart` | boolean | `false` | Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. |

#### Example

```
{
  "name": "scrapeHtml",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "browserRendering": true,
    "warmStart": true,
    "waitForSelector": "body",
    "timeout": 120,
    "maxRetries": 0
  }
}
```

#### Response

The default response body is HTML text. Additional controls can cause the API to return JSON; the returned structure is preserved.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>",
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `scrapeMarkdown`

Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON.

The request sets `markdown=true` and `screenshot=false`. Setting `html` to
`true` also sets `browserRendering=true`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| `timeout` | integer | `300` | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| `geoCode` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| `proxyCountry` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| `super` | boolean | `false` | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| `waitUntil` | string: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle0`, `networkidle2` | `"domcontentloaded"` | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |
| `proxy` | string | Omitted | Custom proxy URL used to load the page. |
| `maxRetries` | integer | Omitted | Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. |
| `saveResult` | boolean | `false` | Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. |
| `blockResources` | boolean | `false` | Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. |
| `waitForSelector` | string | Omitted | Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. |
| `returnCookie` | boolean | `false` | Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. |
| `browserRendering` | boolean | `false` | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| `warmStart` | boolean | `false` | Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. |
| `html` | boolean | `false` | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |

#### Example

```
{
  "name": "scrapeMarkdown",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "html": true,
    "warmStart": true
  }
}
```

#### Response

The default response body is Markdown text. Enabling HTML returns JSON containing both HTML and Markdown.

**With html enabled**

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "html": "<html>...</html>",
    "markdown": "# Example page\n\n..."
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

**Default Markdown text**

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": "# Example page\n\nExample Markdown content...",
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "text/markdown; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `getScreenshot`

Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled.

The request always sets `browserRendering=true`, so this tool has no
`browserRendering` input.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| `timeout` | integer | `300` | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| `geoCode` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| `proxyCountry` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| `super` | boolean | `false` | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| `waitUntil` | string: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle0`, `networkidle2` | `"domcontentloaded"` | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |
| `proxy` | string | Omitted | Custom proxy URL used to load the page. |
| `maxRetries` | integer | Omitted | Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. |
| `saveResult` | boolean | `false` | Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. |
| `blockResources` | boolean | `false` | Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. |
| `waitForSelector` | string | Omitted | Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. |
| `returnCookie` | boolean | `false` | Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. |
| `screenshot` | string: `full`, `top` | `"full"` | Screenshot area to capture: full for the entire page or top for the top viewport. |
| `html` | boolean | `true` | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |
| `markdown` | boolean | `false` | Whether to include the page Markdown in the response. |

#### Example

```
{
  "name": "getScreenshot",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "screenshot": "top",
    "html": false,
    "markdown": true
  }
}
```

#### Response

The response body contains a base64 screenshot and requested page outputs. The API can still include HTML when HTML output is disabled.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "html": "<html>...</html>",
    "screenshot": "BASE64_PNG_DATA",
    "markdown": "# Example page\n\n..."
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `scrapeBrand`

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |

The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. It is not a service parameter.

The request uses `action=brand-scraping` and `bundle=none`; page controls are
not accepted.

#### Example

```
{
  "name": "scrapeBrand",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```

#### Response

The API body contains message and a data object with job\_id, status, url, final\_url, brand, and error. Brand details are available at data.data.brand in the response envelope.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "data": {
      "job_id": "JOB_ID",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "final_url": "https://example.com",
      "brand": {
        "name": "Example brand",
        "colors": {
          "background": "#ffffff",
          "text": "#222222"
        },
        "typography": {
          "body": {
            "font_family": "Example font"
          }
        }
      },
      "error": null,
      "bundle_url": null
    },
    "message": "Example response"
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

### `scrapeJson`

Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| `timeout` | integer | `300` | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| `geoCode` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| `proxyCountry` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| `super` | boolean | `false` | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| `waitUntil` | string: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle0`, `networkidle2` | `"domcontentloaded"` | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |

| `prompt` | string | `"Extract all data as complete as possible."` | Instructions describing the data to extract. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |

# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.

The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.

## Getting Your API Token

API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.

Sign in to your MrScraper Dashboard.

Click your **profile icon** in the top-right corner and select **API Tokens** (or go to app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens).

Click **New Token**.

Enter a descriptive **token name** and choose an **expiration date**.

Click **Create**, then copy and securely store the generated token.

Keep Your Token Secure

Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never expose your token in client-side code (like browsers or mobile apps), and store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration.

## Authenticating Requests

Include your API token in the `x-api-token` HTTP header on every request:

```
x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

### Marketplace Endpoints

For Marketplace endpoints, authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 `Authorization` header with a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

## Verify Token

To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the `/subscription-accounts` endpoint:

```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

## Analytics Authentication

Analytics endpoints authenticate using the same `x-api-token` header as all other API endpoints.

When querying analytics, you can also pass the `apiTokenName` query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it:

```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

Note

The `apiTokenName` query parameter filters metrics by the token's name (e.g., `production-worker`).

## Introduction

The MrScraper API provides a powerful and flexible way to programmatically scrape web pages and retrieve structured data. ### Response Headers

Track token usage, bandwidth usage, execution runtime, and target status codes in response headers. See the Response Headers page for details.

# Python SDK

Install and use mrscraper-sdk, the async Python client for the MrScraper API, to retrieve pages as HTML, Markdown, or screenshots, extract brand details and structured JSON, search the web, and check account status.

The mrscraper-sdk is an async Python client for the seven MrScraper services. Its methods share their descriptions, parameter meanings, and defaults with the MCP server, the CLI, the Node.js SDK, and the other integrations. All client methods are **async** and must be awaited with `asyncio` or another async runtime.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. |
| `scrape_html` | Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. |
| `scrape_markdown` | Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. |
| `get_screenshot` | Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. |
| `scrape_brand` | Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. |
| `scrape_json` | Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |
| `web_search` | Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. |

## Requirements

* **Python 3.9 or later**
* Basic familiarity with async/await syntax in Python

Package Information

This page documents version **0.11.0**. Version 0.11.0 replaces `scraper_api` with `scrape_html`, `scrape_markdown`, and `get_screenshot`, replaces `account` with `status`, and adds `scrape_brand` and `scrape_json`. See Migrating from 0.9.x. See mrscraper-sdk on PyPI for the latest release, version history, and metadata.

## Installation

```
python -m pip install --upgrade mrscraper-sdk
```

Import the client in your Python code:

```
from mrscraper import MrScraper
```

## Authentication

Get an API key from the MrScraper app and set it as an environment variable:

```
export MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN="YOUR_TOKEN"
```

Use `MrScraper()` to read the environment, or `MrScraper(token="YOUR_TOKEN")` to pass the key explicitly. The client uses a nonempty `token` first, then `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN`, then `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`. Authentication belongs to the client and is not a method parameter.

For more information on generating API tokens, see the Generate Token guide.

Custom HTTP client

Pass `http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(...)` to reuse a connection pool. You manage the lifetime of a client you supply; otherwise the SDK creates and closes its own. Each service's HTTP deadline still applies with a shared client.

```
import asyncio
import httpx
from mrscraper import MrScraper

async def main():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as http_client:
        client = MrScraper(http_client=http_client)
        print((await client.status())["data"])
        print((await client.scrape_markdown("https://example.com"))["data"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Quick Start

```
import asyncio
from mrscraper import MrScraper

async def main():
    client = MrScraper()
    result = await client.scrape_html(
        "https://example.com",
        browser_rendering=True,
        warm_start=True,
        wait_for_selector="body",
        timeout=120,
        max_retries=0,
    )
    print(result["data"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

Examples use `example.com` as the sample target. Replace it for your use case. Scraping and search calls use tokens from your plan. Inside a notebook with a running event loop, use `await main()` instead of `asyncio.run(main())`.

## Response Format

Every method returns a dictionary:

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status_code` | int | HTTP status code of the API response |
| `data` | Any | The API response body. JSON becomes Python values, text stays a `str`, and binary bodies become `bytes` |
| `headers` | dict | Response headers. Sensitive headers are removed for `status` |

Field names inside `data` are returned as the API sends them and are not converted to snake\_case.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>",
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

Response examples below show selected keys with placeholder values. Actual responses may contain additional fields.

## Shared Parameters

The first argument is the target URL (or the search query for `web_search`). Other parameters are keyword arguments in snake\_case. Optional controls set to `None` are omitted from the request; explicit `False` and `0` are sent as given. You can unpack a dictionary of options with `**payload`.

### Page controls

`scrape_html`, `scrape_markdown`, `get_screenshot`, and `scrape_json` accept these arguments.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | str | Required | Absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL of the page to process. |
| `timeout` | int | `300` | Page load timeout in seconds, from 1 to 300. The HTTP request allows 30 additional seconds. |
| `geo_code` | str | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to load the page from, sent in lowercase. |
| `proxy_country` | str | `"us"` | Two-letter country code of the proxy server, sent in lowercase. |
| `super` | bool | `False` | Whether to route the request through real devices. |
| `wait_until` | str: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle0`, `networkidle2` | `"domcontentloaded"` | Navigation completion event to wait for: domcontentloaded, load, networkidle0, or networkidle2. |
| `proxy` | str | `None` | Custom proxy URL used to load the page. |
| `max_retries` | int | `None` | Maximum number of retries, as a nonnegative integer. Omit this parameter for no limit. |
| `save_result` | bool | `False` | Whether to save the result to the dashboard Result tab. |

### Loading controls

`scrape_html`, `scrape_markdown`, and `get_screenshot` also accept these arguments. `scrape_json` does not.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `block_resources` | bool | `False` | Whether to block images, fonts, and stylesheets while loading the page. |
| `wait_for_selector` | str | `None` | Wait for the page to contain the specified CSS selector before returning the result. |
| `return_cookie` | bool | `False` | Whether to include browser session cookies in the response. |

Browser rendering is optional for HTML, Markdown, and JSON; screenshots always enable it. Markdown with HTML also enables browser rendering.

## Methods

### `status`

Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. It takes no service parameters, and its HTTP deadline is fixed at 600 seconds.

```
import asyncio
from mrscraper import MrScraper

async def main():
    result = await MrScraper().status()
    account = result["data"]["data"]
    print(account["tokenUsage"], account["tokenLimit"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

The API body contains `message` and `data`. Account details remain nested in `data`, including `subscriptionItem` and `scraperAllowance`, so the response exposes them at `result["data"]["data"]`.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "message": "Example response",
    "data": {
      "id": "ACCOUNT_ID",
      "tokenLimit": 100000,
      "tokenUsage": 2500,
      "stripeStatus": "active",
      "user": {
        "name": "Example user",
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "isVerified": true
      },
      "subscriptionItem": {
        "name": "Example plan",
        "tokenLimit": 100000
      },
      "scraperAllowance": {
        "remaining": 97500,
        "plans": [{ "remaining": 97500 }]
      }
    }
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `scrape_html`

Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional.

Accepts page controls, loading controls, and:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `browser_rendering` | bool | `False` | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| `warm_start` | bool | `False` | Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. |

```
result = await client.scrape_html(
    "https://example.com",
    browser_rendering=True,
    wait_for_selector="body",
)
print(result["data"])
```

The default response body is HTML text. Additional controls can cause the API to return JSON; the returned structure is preserved.

### `scrape_markdown`

Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON.

Accepts page controls, loading controls, and:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `browser_rendering` | bool | `False` | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| `warm_start` | bool | `False` | Whether to enable warm start for more reliable scraping, at the cost of additional latency. |
| `html` | bool | `False` | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |

```
result = await client.scrape_markdown("https://example.com", html=True, warm_start=True)
print(result["data"]["markdown"])
```

The default response body is Markdown text. With `html=True`, `data` is a dictionary containing both outputs:

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "html": "<html>...</html>",
    "markdown": "# Example page\n\n..."
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

### `get_screenshot`

Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled.

Accepts page controls, loading controls, and:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `screenshot` | str: `full`, `top` | `"full"` | Screenshot area to capture: full for the entire page or top for the top viewport. |
| `html` | bool | `True` | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |
| `markdown` | bool | `False` | Whether to include the page Markdown in the response. |

```
import base64

result = await client.get_screenshot("https://example.com", screenshot="top", html=False)
with open("page.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(result["data"]["screenshot"]))
```

The response body contains a base64 screenshot and the requested page outputs. The API can still include HTML when HTML output is disabled.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "html": "<html>...</html>",
    "screenshot": "BASE64_PNG_DATA",
    "markdown": "# Example page\n\n..."
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

### `scrape_brand`

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. It takes only the URL; page controls are not accepted. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds.

```
result = await client.scrape_brand("https://example.com")
print(result["data"]["data"]["brand"])
```

The API body contains `message` and a `data` object with `job_id`, `status`, `url`, `final_url`, `brand`, and `error`. Brand details are at `result["data"]["data"]["brand"]`.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "data": {
      "job_id": "JOB_ID",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "url": "https://example.com",
      "final_url": "https://example.com",
      "brand": {
        "name": "Example brand",
        "colors": { "background": "#ffffff", "text": "#222222" },
        "typography": { "body": { "font_family": "Example font" } }
      },
      "error": null,
      "bundle_url": null
    },
    "message": "Example response"
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

### `scrape_json`

Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output.

Accepts page controls and:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | str | `"Extract all data as complete as possible."` | Instructions describing the data to extract. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |
| `browser_rendering` | bool | `False` | Whether to render the page in a browser before returning the result. |
| `html` | bool | `False` | Whether to include the page HTML in the response. |
| `screenshot` | bool | `False` | Whether to include a base64 screenshot in the response. |

```
result = await client.scrape_json(
    "https://example.com",
    prompt='Extract the first 2 items with title and price. Json Schema: {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"price":{"type":"string"}},"required":["title","price"]}}',
    browser_rendering=True,
)
print(result["data"]["data"])
```

Extraction results are in the API body's `data` field and follow the requested schema. Response metadata includes `thread_id`, `token_usage`, `status`, `error`, `runtime`, and `cookies`. `html`, `markdown`, and `screenshot` can be empty strings when not requested.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "success": true,
    "data": [{ "title": "Example item", "price": "10.00" }],
    "thread_id": "THREAD_ID",
    "token_usage": 1,
    "html": "",
    "markdown": "",
    "screenshot": "",
    "status": "Results ready",
    "error": "",
    "runtime": 1.23,
    "cookies": []
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json"
  }
}
```

### `web_search`

Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. The first argument is the search query. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | str | Required | Search query text, trimmed before sending, containing 1 to 1000 characters. |
| `country` | str | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to search from, sent in lowercase. |
| `num_results` | int | `10` | Number of search results to request, as an integer from 10 to 100. Fewer results may be returned. |

```
result = await client.web_search("site:example.com documentation", country="id", num_results=20)
for item in result["data"]["data"]:
    print(item["rank"], item["title"], item["url"])
```

The API body contains `success`, `message`, a `data` array, and `tokenUsage`. Each result includes `rank`, `title`, `url`, `description`, and `source`.

```
{
  "status_code": 200,
  "data": {
    "success": true,
    "message": "Example response",
    "data": [
      {
        "rank": 1,
        "title": "Example result",
        "url": "https://example.com",
        "description": "Example result description.",
        "source": "example.com"
      }
    ],
    "tokenUsage": 1
  },
  "headers": {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  }
}
```

## Error Handling

Invalid arguments raise `ValueError` or `TypeError` before any request is sent. Request failures raise these exceptions, all subclasses of `MrScraperError`:

| Exception | When It's Raised |
| --- | --- |
| `AuthenticationError` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `APIError` | Any other HTTP error status. `status_code` contains the HTTP status when available |
| `NetworkError` | Connection or timeout failures |

```
import asyncio
from mrscraper import MrScraper, APIError, AuthenticationError, NetworkError

async def main():
    try:
        await MrScraper().scrape_html("https://example.com")
    except AuthenticationError as error:
        print("Check authentication:", error)
    except APIError as error:
        print(error.status_code, error)
    except NetworkError as error:
        print("Request failed:", error)

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Troubleshooting

* If authentication fails, check the token precedence described in Authentication.
* Use snake\_case argument names, not the camelCase HTTP field names.
* Page timeouts are integers from 1 to 300. `status`, `scrape_brand`, and `web_search` have fixed deadlines and do not accept a timeout.
* Inspect the raw API body before selecting nested fields.

## Migrating from Earlier Versions

### From 0.9.x

Version 0.11.0 replaces the three 0.9.x methods with seven service methods.

| 0.9.x | 0.11.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `client.scraper_api(url)` | `client.scrape_html(url)` |
| `client.scraper_api(url, html=False, markdown=True)` | `client.scrape_markdown(url)` |
| `client.scraper_api(url, html=True, markdown=True)` | `client.scrape_markdown(url, html=True)` |
| `client.scraper_api(url, html=False, screenshot=True)` | `client.get_screenshot(url, html=False)` |
| `client.scraper_api(url, home_page=True)` | `client.scrape_html(url, warm_start=True)` |
| `client.account()` | `client.status()` |

* `status` returns the raw API body. The normalized 0.9.x summary fields such as `token_remaining` and `usage_percent` are gone; read `result["data"]["data"]` instead.
* `status` and `web_search` no longer accept a `timeout` argument.
* Defaults changed: page `timeout` is now `300`, `geo_code` and `proxy_country` default to `"us"`, and an omitted `max_retries` means no limit.
* `use_proxy`, `bypass_proxy`, `cookie_jar`, `headers`, `token_cap`, `stream`, and `discard_token_secret` are no longer accepted.
* `scrape_brand` and `scrape_json` are new.

### Earlier versions

* **0.7.x to 0.9.0:** the format-specific 0.7.x methods were merged into `scraper_api`. Upgrade directly to the 0.11.0 methods above.
* **0.6.0 to 0.7.x:** `web_search` moved to `action: "websearch"` with `country` and `num_results`.
* **0.5.0 to 0.6.0:** added `account`.
* **0.4.0 to 0.5.0:** `fetch_content` was renamed `scraper_api`.
* **0.3.x and earlier:** `fetch_html` and the AI scraper, manual scraper, results, and analytics methods were removed. For scrapers, results, and analytics, call the REST API directly.

## Migration from Firecrawl

If you're migrating from the Firecrawl Python SDK, use this mapping to find equivalent MrScraper methods.

| Firecrawl Method | MrScraper Equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Scrape a URL with HTML output | `scrape_html` |
| Scrape a URL with Markdown output | `scrape_markdown` |
| Scrape a URL with a screenshot | `get_screenshot` |
| Scrape a URL with JSON extraction | `scrape_json` |
| Scrape a URL with branding | `scrape_brand` |
| Search | `web_search` |

Discover how our powerful scraping platform can transform the way you extract data. Whether you're scraping e-commerce product data, collecting job listings, gathering customer reviews for sentiment analysis, or extracting any website content, our AI scrapers and workflows are designed to automate and simplify the process, giving you a powerful edge in any project.

New to MrScraper? These pages get you from sign-up to your first scraped dataset.

### Quickstart

Run your first scraper in a few minutes with a step-by-step walkthrough.

### Web Search

Run a search query and get ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources.

### Scraper API

# Workflow API Access

Learn how to run any scraper you have created through a MrScraper API endpoint, so you can automate scraping or integrate it into your application.

MrScraper lets you run any scraper you've created directly through an API endpoint. This is useful when you want to automate scraping, integrate it into your application, or test requests in tools like Postman.

## How to Run a Scraper Through the API

### Setup Steps

Open your dashboard and select a scraper you've already created. If you don't have one yet, create it first.

In the scraper window, click **Settings**.

Select **AI Scraper API Access** and slide to activate it.

Note

This turns off the AI chat for this scraper and enables API mode.

After activation, copy the example API request shown on the page.

Paste the request into Postman (or another API tool).

Note

You can replace the URL with any URL you want to scrape.

You can also run the scraper directly from Rerun an AI Scraper endpoint.

## API Request Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Location | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-api-token` | string | header | Yes | - | Your MrScraper API token |
| `scraperId` | string | body | Yes | - | The unique ID of the scraper you activated |
| `url` | string | body | Yes | - | The webpage URL you want to scrape |
| `maxRetry` | integer | body | No | `3` | Number of retry attempts if the scraping fails |
| `maxPages` | integer | body | No | 0 | Maximum number of pages to scrape (useful for listing/pagination). Use this to control how many pages you want to extract from multi-page listings |
| `timeout` | integer | body | No | `None` | Request timeout in seconds. Increase this value if you're scraping many pages or complex websites |
| `stream` | boolean | body | No | `false` | Enable streaming response mode. **Highly recommended when scraping multiple pages** that may take several minutes. If the connection is interrupted mid-process, you'll still receive the partial data that was already scraped from completed pages |

About maxPages

If the website has fewer pages than maxPages, it will scrape all available pages.

## Example Request Body

### Basic Single-Page Scraper

```
{
  "scraperId": "1c9f4043-b572-462a-ab94-a330672f1af5",
  "url": "https://example.com/property",
  "maxRetry": 3,
  "maxPages": 1,
  "timeout": 300,
  "stream": false
}
```

### Listing Agent API (Multi-Page Scraper)

When scraping listings or paginated content, use the `maxPages` parameter:

```
{
  "scraperId": "1c9f4043-b572-462a-ab94-a330672f1af5",
  "url": "https://www.zillow.com/ky/",
  "maxRetry": 3,
  "maxPages": 4,
  "timeout": 1100,
  "stream": false
}
```

Tip

**Timeout Guidelines:**

* For single-page scraping: 300-600 seconds is usually sufficient
* For multi-page scraping: Increase timeout proportionally to `maxPages` (e.g., 1100+ seconds for 4+ pages)
* If you encounter timeout errors, increase the `timeout` value

### Scraping with Streaming Response

```
{
  "scraperId": "your-scraper-id",
  "url": "https://example.com/search",
  "maxRetry": 3,
  "maxPages": 10,
  "timeout": 2000,
  "stream": true
}
```

Important

**When to Use `stream: true`:**

* When scraping multiple pages (`maxPages` > 1) that may take several minutes
* For long-running scraping jobs to prevent data loss
* If connection interruptions occur mid-process, you'll still receive partial data from pages that were already scraped
* Ensures you don't lose all progress if the request is interrupted before completion

## Common Use Cases

### Scraping a Single Product Page

```
{
  "scraperId": "your-scraper-id",
  "url": "https://shop.example.com/product/123",
  "maxRetry": 2
}
```

### Scraping Real Estate Listings (Multiple Pages)

```
{
  "scraperId": "your-scraper-id",
  "url": "https://www.zillow.com/ky/",
  "maxRetry": 3,
  "maxPages": 10,
  "timeout": 2000,
  "stream": true
}
```

Tip

For multi-page scraping, always set `stream: true` to ensure you receive data from completed pages even if the process is interrupted.

## Best Practices

1. **Start with lower `maxPages` values** and increase gradually to test performance
2. **Adjust timeout based on website complexity** and number of pages
3. **Use `stream: true` for multi-page scraping** to prevent data loss if the connection is interrupted
4. **Use appropriate retry values** (3 is recommended for most cases)
5. **Monitor your API usage** to stay within rate limits
6. **Test with a single page first** before running large batch operations

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Timeout errors | Increase the `timeout` parameter, especially when using `maxPages` |
| Failed requests | Check `maxRetry` value and ensure your API token is valid |
| Incomplete data from listings | Increase `maxPages` or verify the URL structure |
| Rate limiting | Reduce concurrent requests or contact support for higher limits |

Need Help?

If you encounter issues or need assistance with API integration, contact our support team or check the API Reference for detailed endpoint documentation.
